groups.A: Known rule, new wording (EventBridge, RDS Proxy/Aurora, DX gateway, Redshift snapshot copy, placement group, SSM parameters)
groups.B: Storage & performance fit (DynamoDB key/table design, EFS vs Lambda/OpenSearch, sharding/cache vs IOPS)
groups.C: Cost choice (reserved capacity, Spot Fleet mix, RI sharing by AZ, Fargate+Spot)
groups.D: Near-identical options - one phrase decides (CodeDeploy extra, Lambda/SQS vs Step Functions, behavior vs ALB rule)
groups.E: Service fit / app design (AppSync, Client VPN, MGN, ENI licenses, cert at ALB, WorkDocs, NLB+NACL, DB replication)

5.keywords: CreateUser, auto remove permissions, notify security team; select three
5.trap: 🔁 Picked E (CloudTrail cannot send SNS notifications) and F (EventBridge cannot invoke Fargate tasks directly); missed the EventBridge CreateUser rule (A) and Step Functions (C).
5.rule: CloudTrail API event -> EventBridge rule -> Step Functions (remediate) + SNS (notify). CloudTrail alone does not notify.

13.keywords: 20,000 sensors every 15 min, query one sensor past week, delete older than 8 weeks, cost-effective DynamoDB
13.trap: One table forever grows enormous and slows search; deleting old data needs table-per-period. Option C lacks the week split.
13.rule: Time-series DynamoDB: one table per period (drop old whole) with sensor ID partition key + timestamp sort key; never concatenate timestamp into key.

14.keywords: automate testing of CloudFormation templates from private GitHub, prevent bad executions
14.trap: Picked the twin that executes the change set via CodeDeploy, an unneeded service; CodePipeline itself executes the change set and CodeBuild tests.
14.rule: CFN CI/CD = CodePipeline (GitHub source) + change set + CodeBuild tests. CodeDeploy is not for CloudFormation deployment.

15.keywords: re-architect: reduce cost, drop third-party analysis, less management, dynamic web app, SQS workers
15.trap: Picked S3 static website hosting for the web app; S3 has no server-side processing, but the app is dynamic. Fargate web + Spot workers + Rekognition fits.
15.rule: Dynamic web app cannot run on S3 website hosting. Fargate for web, Spot for queue workers, Rekognition for video analysis, S3 for storage.

17.keywords: real-time comments, serverless API Gateway Lambda DynamoDB, reduce comment latency
17.trap: Picked CloudFront caching of API responses; cached comments may not be new, so not real-time. Real-time push needs WebSocket subscriptions.
17.rule: Real-time updates pushed to clients = AWS AppSync GraphQL subscriptions over WebSockets, not caching or polling.

19.keywords: Client VPN for remote employees, existing Site-to-Site VPN and VPC peering, most cost-effective, minimal change
19.trap: Picked installing Client VPN at the data center with Transit Gateway, which reconfigures peering. Client software goes on employee workstations; one endpoint in main account.
19.rule: Client VPN: client on workstations, ONE endpoint in the main account reaching peered VPCs; no Transit Gateway rework needed.

21.keywords: lower DynamoDB cost, predictable daily batch, select two
21.trap: Picked ElastiCache (A) instead of dropping the daily table after the S3 export; reserved capacity plus dropping the old table cut cost, not caching.
21.rule: Predictable DynamoDB throughput: reserved capacity; also drop or expire data already exported to S3 to cut storage cost.

28.keywords: cut RDS Multi-AZ failover from 40s to under 20s, keep connections alive, queue writes; choose three
28.trap: 🔁 Picked E (Redis cache) and F (read replicas on RDS MySQL); caches cannot queue writes and RDS replicas don't give fast failover. Need RDS Proxy + Aurora Multi-AZ replicas.
28.rule: Faster failover, preserved connections, queued writes = RDS Proxy + Aurora with Aurora Replicas. Caches do not queue writes.

29.keywords: 500 physical servers, Windows and Linux, separate staging/launch accounts, migrate off data centers
29.trap: Picked VM Import/Export, which is manual per-server image conversion; MGN replicates physical servers continuously with agent, test launch and cutover.
29.rule: Large-scale physical or virtual server rehost = AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) with replication agent.

34.keywords: legacy app, license tied to MAC address, static DB IPs, new license takes 15 hours
34.trap: Picked B (license baked into one AMI); each instance needs its own MAC-bound license. Need a pool of licensed ENIs (licenses in S3) and DB IPs in Parameter Store.
34.rule: MAC-bound license: pre-license a pool of ENIs, keep license files in S3, attach via bootstrap; config values (DB IPs) in SSM Parameter Store.

38.keywords: 20GB forecast overwritten every 15 min, 1,500 users/s spiking 10x, under 2 seconds
38.trap: Picked OpenSearch + API Gateway + Lambda; Lambda burst concurrency cannot scale fast enough for peak. EFS on Auto Scaling EC2 behind CloudFront with 15-minute cache fits.
38.rule: Spiky high request rate with periodically overwritten data: EFS + Auto Scaling EC2 + ELB + CloudFront cache matching refresh interval; Lambda burst limits.

40.keywords: Reserved + On-Demand EC2 on one instance, recover from zone outage, most cost-effective
40.trap: Picked all On-Demand ASG: resilient but costs more. Spot Fleet mixing On-Demand and Spot across AZs is cheaper while staying available; all-Spot risks interruption.
40.rule: Cheapest multi-AZ resilience = Spot Fleet mixing On-Demand (baseline) and Spot across AZs behind ALB; all-Spot risks interruption.

41.keywords: CloudFront with ALB default origin, S3 static assets with OAC return 404, select two
41.trap: Picked A (ALB path rule to S3); OAC only allows CloudFront to read S3, so ALB cannot serve S3. Fix is in CloudFront: add S3 origin and a path-pattern behavior.
41.rule: OAC-protected S3 content must be reached from CloudFront: add an S3 origin and a path-pattern behavior. ALB cannot forward to S3.

44.keywords: enable SSL on HTTP-only site, separate Development and Security team roles for the certificate
44.trap: Picked CloudHSM on the EC2 instances; clients hit the load balancer, not instances, and CloudHSM adds cost. Store cert in IAM, restrict by policy, terminate SSL at ALB.
44.rule: Separation of duties for SSL cert: store cert in IAM/ACM with IAM policy for Security team and attach it to the ALB, not EC2.

51.keywords: 120GB dataset on PIOPS EBS 3000 IOPS per instance, cut cost without hurting performance or durability
51.trap: Picked 1TB gp2 per instance to reach 3000 IOPS; many 1TB volumes cost more. Shared EFS with Provisioned Throughput is cheaper; Max I/O adds latency.
51.rule: Same dataset duplicated on per-instance EBS: use one shared EFS with Provisioned Throughput mode, not Max I/O (higher latency).

54.keywords: consolidated billing, PROD bought 10 RIs in us-west-2a, DEV runs in us-west-2a, UAT in us-west-1a, who benefits
54.trap: Picked none since PROD has no instances. RI discount applies to other member accounts in the same AZ; only DEV runs in us-west-2a.
54.rule: In consolidated billing, zonal RIs discount matching instances in any member account only if in the same AZ and type.

56.keywords: replicate RDS MySQL to on-premises MySQL for read-only analytics, most secure
56.trap: Picked A (replicate to an EC2 MySQL first), claiming RDS cannot replicate on-premises; a secure IPSec VPN to the VPC makes direct replication to on-premises MySQL feasible.
56.rule: RDS MySQL to on-premises replication: IPSec VPN or VGW, external MySQL as replica, mysqldump seed, start replication. SSL endpoint alone is not it.

57.keywords: cluster controller outside placement group, improve network between it and HPC instances, keep low latency
57.trap: Picked terminating and stopping everything; you only stop the controller, move it into the existing placement group, and restart it. No need to touch others.
57.rule: Move an existing instance into a placement group: stop it, modify placement group, start. No terminate, no ENA/EIP effect on bandwidth.

58.keywords: low latency high bandwidth link from Texas data center to VPCs in US East and US West
58.trap: 🔁 Picked two separate Direct Connect connections (one per VPC), costly; one Direct Connect connection plus a Direct Connect gateway with two VGWs reaches both Regions.
58.rule: One DX connection to multiple VPCs/Regions = Direct Connect gateway with a VGW per VPC and private virtual interfaces.

62.keywords: automate mapping latest AMI IDs in CloudFormation templates
62.trap: Picked CloudFormation with Service Catalog; Service Catalog only manages approved product catalogs and doesn't fetch the latest AMI. Parameter Store parameters resolve AMI IDs.
62.rule: Latest AMI in CloudFormation = SSM Parameter Store parameter type, then update-stack. Not Service Catalog, Config, or State Manager.

63.keywords: Lambda metadata extraction takes 45 min, split by metadata type, reduce extraction time
63.trap: Picked Lambda feeding SQS as Step Functions input; an SQS queue cannot directly invoke a Step Functions workflow. Use a workflow that runs the extraction workflow per photo.
63.rule: SQS cannot be a direct Step Functions input. Parallel state for per-type functions, plus an orchestration workflow iterating over photos.

64.keywords: Redshift RPO 24 hours, RTO 1 hour, survive a Regional outage
64.trap: 🔁 Picked Redshift replication to a secondary-Region cluster with DNS switch; Redshift has no direct replication, only snapshots. Cross-Region snapshot copy is not enabled by default.
64.rule: Redshift DR across Regions = automated snapshots with cross-Region snapshot copy enabled (no cross-Region replication).

65.keywords: UDP gaming service, Shield Advanced enabled, migrate to AWS, select two
65.trap: Picked CloudFront (E), which does not fit a UDP service; WAF can't protect NLB either. Use NLB for UDP and NACL to deny non-UDP.
65.rule: UDP traffic = Network Load Balancer (Layer 4). Block non-UDP with NACLs; WAF and ALB are Layer 7 and don't apply.

66.keywords: slow reads on Multi-AZ RDS MySQL, eventual consistency, budget-optimized instances; select three
66.trap: Picked F (provisioned IOPS): increases IOPS but very expensive. Sharding scales horizontally and is cheaper than upsizing or paying for IOPS.
66.rule: Read-heavy RDS bottleneck on a budget: read replicas + ElastiCache + sharding; avoid costly vertical or Provisioned IOPS upgrades.

74.keywords: secure content management via API, version download, API rollback, external custom apps
74.trap: Picked S3 with client-side encryption and shared keys, a security risk and custom rollback; WorkDocs gives access management, versioning and encryption built in.
74.rule: Document management with versioning, user access control and encryption, API access = Amazon WorkDocs. Never share encryption keys with customers.
